SK-01.c01: The vehicle inspection is the **first** of three skills tests; you walk around your vehicle and show what to check and **why**.
For each item you **name it, point to it or touch it**, and explain out loud what you are looking for.
You must **pass this test first**; if you fail it, the basic control skills and road tests are put off to another day.
**Governor cut-out** is the air pressure where the compressor stops pumping; a **slack adjuster** links the brake chamber pushrod to the brake.
SK-01.c02: **No interpreters**: the whole test is in English; the first **2** language offenses get verbal warnings, the **3rd** on that date is automatic failure.
A vehicle with **marked or labeled parts** cannot be used, and you may not write notes on the inspection guide.
If the **brake lights, emergency flashers, turn signals or horn** don't work, the skills and road tests are postponed.
You get **3 tries in all** to pass the three skills tests.
SK-01.c03: Walking up, look for damage, leaning, fresh **leaks** under the vehicle, and hazards; the parking brake must be set or wheels chocked.
Oil and power steering fluid must be **above the refill mark**; hydraulic brake fluid **between the add and full marks**.
A snug belt has **1/2 to 3/4 inch** of play at its center, with no cracks, frays or wear.
If a part is **not belt-driven**, tell the examiner which one and check that it works and is secure.
Safe start: **Neutral** (or Park), clutch in, start, hold the clutch until idle, then release it slowly.
SK-01.c04: Build air to **governor cut-out**, about **120–140 psi** (or the maker's figure); oil pressure and temperature gauges should rise to normal.
Emergency equipment: spare electrical fuses, **3 red reflective triangles** (or 6 fuses or 3 liquid-burning flares), and a charged, mounted fire extinguisher.
**Tire chains**, tire-changing equipment, emergency phone numbers and an accident reporting kit are only optional.
Clearance lights and reflectors are **red on the rear, amber elsewhere**; check brake lights, turn signals and 4-way flashers **separately**.
SK-01.c05: Hydraulic brakes: **pump 3 times, hold 5 seconds**; the pedal must not sink, and skipping either part is **automatic failure**.
Air brake checks must be done and the numbers said; doing them wrong is **automatic failure of the entire vehicle inspection**.
Applied leakage in 1 minute: max **3 psi** single, **4 psi** combination of 2, **6 psi** combination of 3 or more.
The low air warning must come on **before 55 psi**; the parking brake knob normally pops out at **20–45 psi**.
Service brake check: roll at about **5 mph** and brake; the vehicle should stop and **not pull** to either side.
SK-01.c06: Steering box and linkage: mounted securely, not leaking, no worn joints and **no missing nuts, bolts or cotter keys**.
The vehicle is **out of service** when **1/4 or more** of the leaf springs are missing or broken.
A manual slack adjuster's pushrod should **not move more than 1 inch** when pulled by hand with brakes released.
Brake chambers, hoses, drums and linings must not leak or be cracked, and linings must not be **dangerously thin**; check every axle.
SK-01.c07: Tread depth must be at least **4/32 inch** on steering-axle tires and **2/32 inch** on all other tires.
Check inflation with a **tire gauge**; kicking a tire or hitting it with a mallet earns **no credit**.
Don't mix radial and bias-ply tires, and **bus front tires** may not be recapped, retreaded or regrooved.
**Rust trails or shiny threads** can mean loose lug nuts; rims may have no welding repairs.
With after-treatment, the **DEF tank** must be **more than 1/8 full** and its dash indicator must work.
SK-01.c08: Trailer air connectors must be sealed, the **electrical plug seated and locked**, and air lines free of leaks with no steel braid showing.
Look into the fifth-wheel gap: the **locking jaws** must be fully closed around the **kingpin**.
The trailer must lie flat on a greased skid plate with **no gap**, and the release arm engaged with its safety latch in place.
Sliding fifth wheel pins must be **fully engaged**, positioned so the tractor frame clears the landing gear in turns.
SK-01.c09: A school bus driver also checks an **emergency kit** and a **body fluid cleanup kit**, plus the usual emergency equipment.
Check the flashing amber and red lights, strobe and **stop arm** (if equipped), which must extend fully, plus student mirrors.
The entry door must close securely from inside, and a **handicap lift** must be fully retracted and latched with a working interlock.
**Demonstrate at least 1** emergency exit, and point out and describe all the others.
SK-01.c10: Trailer front: **glad hands locked** and not leaking, electrical plug seated; header board secure and no missing rivets.
Trailer side: **landing gear fully raised**, and tandem release arm and locking pins locked.
Coach/transit bus: demonstrate **at least 1** emergency exit, and check that the bus **sits level** with no suspension air leaks.
Check bus baggage doors latch, and batteries are secure with **cell caps present** and no heavy corrosion.
SK-01.c11: Class A gets **1 of 4** equal versions; Class B or C gets **1 of 3**; you learn which just **before** the test.
Class A always includes engine start, the in-cab inspection and the **coupling system**; B and C include any special features.
The examiner may test the whole vehicle **or only part** of it, and explains which.
You must **pass the inspection before** moving on to the basic control skills test.
